correctness.rationale: Modulo constants, input adjacent differences are the coefficients of suffix steps, so the exact induced variation norm of the derivative is the largest variation of a step column. A full column is 0,p,q,1; a truncated column has no greater variation. Set X=u_(k-1), Y=u_k for the two shared exponentials. The only possible decrease p-q is bounded by P-Q=(ac-b²)XY/((bX+cY)(aX+bY)). When this is positive, minimizing the denominator divided by XY gives (sqrt(ac)+b)² at X/Y=sqrt(c/a). Integrating derivatives along the input segment proves the two-input bound. The cut k=4 exists already at n=6 and places both outside values 0 and 1 in the output. In the nonexpansive regime the column is monotone at all finite base points, so a finite suffix step gives equality. In the expansive regime sending the two nonshared exponentials to zero yields the extreme derivative value in the limit; small finite perturbations then approach it. On every fixed finite segment the shared-mass bound is strict at all potentially descending columns, uniformly by continuity and compactness; hence no finite attainment. Temperature independence follows also from F_tau(x)=tau F_1(x/tau). Independent exact tests of finite pairs use rational exponentials and compare powers of products of adjacent ratios, without evaluating logarithms.
residual_risks: Frozen test output labels a group as temperature tests although the shown calls use the default temperature. The independent scaling identity proves temperature independence. Shorter paths and more than three taps are outside the claim.

value.rationale: This is a natural two-signal stability problem for a nonlinear local smoother. The threshold alone would leave the severity and realizability of instability unanswered. The exact gain from one overlap reversal, its near-three limit for a small middle tap, and a strict distinction between finite equality and concentration in the limit answer those questions within a complete three-tap classification.
residual_risks: The result does not classify arbitrary filters, weighted seminorms or cyclic geometries.
